script.base: Spread and total were not saved, so this flow is inferred only from form, not from the book's implied totals or who the book expects to lead. SF's defense is the stopper in the pack (3.79 YPC, 3 runs of 10+, 4 passes of 20+ on 108 attempts) and DEN's is the leak (5.30 YPC, 9 runs of 10+, 11 passes of 20+ on 117). Base case: SF moves the ball, especially if DEN blitzes at 38% into Purdy's +1.37 EPA vs blitz (n=25), and is level or ahead after halftime. DEN does not establish Dobbins (L3 35 carries, 121 yards, 3.46 YPC) against that front and stays near 10-14 carries, while Waddle's 247 air yards do not become the explosives SF has not allowed. Pace and garbage time are unknown without a total.
script.flip1: DEN leads early and stays ahead, so the run game is the clock. Dobbins' carry count jumps toward the high teens while Coleman (10 L3 carries) mixes in less, and 17 carries at SF's 3.79 YPC is about 64 yards, which busts the rush under. Waddle's under can still hold if a leading DEN runs instead of hunting 20+ yard shots.
script.flip2: DEN's 38% blitz does not bother Purdy (already +1.37 EPA vs blitz) and the game turns into the explosive SF offense the L3 hints at (Kittle 174 rec yards, Evans 137, Purdy 94 rush yards on 9 carries). Waddle's 7 targets per game become 9+ and one chunk play clears 58 even if SF's 20+ rate stays low. Dobbins' under still holds because a trailing DEN abandons the run and his 11.7-carry pace shrinks.

DEN bleeds the run and explosives: 5.30 rush YPC, 9 runs of 10+, and 11 passes of 20+ on 117 attempts, with the middle (8.56 YPA) and left (7.78) the soft pass locations.
matchup.overlap: Anti-overlap is the DEN leg: Waddle is the primary target (21 targets, 247 air yards, 150 rec yards) and he attacks the deep area SF has not given up (4 of 20+). That is the under, not an over. True overlap the other way: Kittle (16 targets, 174 yards, 142 air) and Evans (16 targets, 137 yards, 175 air) attack the explosive and intermediate areas DEN gives up, and CMC's 4.74 YPC overlaps DEN's 5.30 YPC allowed. Those overs are not taken because the posted rungs sit above recent pace (Kittle 58.0 vs 64.5, CMC rush 55.3 vs 65.5, CMC rush+rec 90.0 vs 112.5).

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both unders lost because the unposted spread was wrong and DEN controlled the game. Dobbins got 18-20 carries, Coleman did not steal the 10-carry share he had in the L3, and one 15-yard run plus a 3.8 YPC grind cleared 59.5 even though SF's season rate is 3.79 — three games of run defense is a small sample and a positive script was the kill we already named. Waddle did not need a 20+ yard bomb: 8 targets at his 7.1 yards per target, or one 25-yard crosser plus his usual underneath, cleared 58, and the +nan price meant the number was stale or unbettable. The same Monday, SF's explosive suppression was just who they had faced, not a trait that travels, so the air-yard story was a three-game mirage.
slip_story: One story only: SF's defense caps DEN. Dobbins rush under and Waddle rec under win together if the 3.79 YPC front and the 4-of-108 explosive rate travel. Dobbins is script-dependent on DEN not leading with a heavy carry count (dies on flip 1, holds on flip 2). Waddle is script-dependent on no shootout (holds on flip 1, dies on flip 2). Do not add CMC, Kittle, or Evans overs: those need DEN's leak (5.30 YPC, 11 explosives, middle 8.56 YPA) and a Purdy-vs-blitz spike, which is a different stack and the shootout flip that kills Waddle. Do not add Harvey rec or rush+rec overs; his -33 air yards are checkdowns that show up only if DEN is behind, and that is not required for these two legs.
